LESSON: HUMAN CIRCULATORY SYSTEM

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Living things and the Environment
Topic 1.3: Human circulatory system
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Human circulatory system, part of Living things and the Environment in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Which are the main parts of the human circulatory system? 2. How can we keep the human circulatory system healthy?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Use print and non-print materials to search for information on the main parts of the human circulatory system and share the finding with peers. Those who may not turn pages to use page turners or be supported by 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Use print and non-print materials to search for information on the main parts of the human circulatory system and share the finding with peers. Those who may not turn pages to use page turners or be supported by 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Human circulatory system together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: The learner acquires listening and speaking skills as they discuss components of

blood and their functions.

● Digital literacy: The learner uses interactive platforms or digital images as they search for information on the main parts

of the human circulatory system and share the finding with peers.

Values:
● Responsibility: The learner learns how to live responsibly while practising ways for maintaining a healthy circulatory

system.

● Unity: The learner respects others opinions as they collaboratively discuss and develop a routine plan on maintaining a

healthy human circulatory system.

9

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Health promotion issues: The learner learns ways of living healthy as they discusses ways of maintaining a healthy human

circulatory system and develops a routine for maintaining a healthy circulatory system.

Links to other Learning Areas:
● The learner is able to link information on common health conditions of the human circulatory system to lifestyle diseases in

Agriculture and Nutrition.

● The learner is able to relate modelling of the human circulatory system to modelling in Creative arts and Sports.
